issues.title: Decide: deploy the photos API, and whether it may analyze images (OWNER-ACTIONS.md item 22, never tracked as an issue)
issues.body:
`photos/` stores private before/after photos per micro zone for the web app, built 2026-10-14, independently security-reviewed and hardened 2026-10-15, still not deployed. Full contract in PHOTOS-API.md, reasoning in DECISIONS.md D-032. 37 end-to-end checks pass, including that GPS metadata is stripped and that an invented root cause or step is thrown out.

An independent security review (not the session that built it) found and fixed four real gaps: a decompression-bomb memory DoS, a financial-DoS gap (unlimited vision-API spend via session/address rotation), a disk-exhaustion DoS that would also have taken down the other two businesses sharing the VPS, and rate limits that silently reset on restart. All four are fixed and proved fail-then-pass.

The frontend (`site/photo-check.html`) exists, renders every model field with `textContent` not `innerHTML` (closing an XSS risk the review named as open pending a frontend), and is deliberately unlinked and noindexed pending this decision.

Two decisions, both Phil's:
1. Deploy it? Adds one small container on the VPS, reachable only through the site's nginx at `/api/photos/`, holding customer photos in its own volume. Without a vision key it still stores photos and returns each zone's published steps, clearly marked "no image was analyzed".
2. Let it analyze images? Needs an Anthropic API key with a monthly spend limit set first (each analysis is one image call; the service also caps each session at 20/day).

Recommendation: deploy without vision analysis first (decision 1 alone, zero ongoing cost, the harder security work is already done and independently reviewed), and defer decision 2 until there is real usage to justify the spend.

issues.title: Decide: run a public MCP endpoint, or retire the unused mcp/ build entirely (OWNER-ACTIONS.md item 21, never tracked as an issue)
issues.body:
This repository has built and published an MCP server image on every content change since 2026-08-31, and keeps a byte-identical 1.1 MB copy of the whole corpus in `mcp/content.json` with a preflight gate enforcing it. Checked against production over ssh on 2026-09-30: it has never run. No `6s-mcp` container exists, port 8974 is not listening, the image was never even pulled to the host, and no file names an endpoint a client could connect to.

An MCP endpoint would let an AI assistant query the 114 zones, diagnoses, standards and kit lists directly as structured data. The access log already shows retrieval crawlers for three AI products fetching this site (OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, GPTBot), so the audience is not hypothetical.

Why this needs a decision rather than just starting it: exposing it puts a new unauthenticated listening service on a VPS that also runs Ledgerium AI and Compassion Benchmark, someone else's revenue-bearing infrastructure. The content is already public, so this is not about disclosure, it is about adding a process on a shared box.

Capacity is checked, not assumed: as of 2026-09-30 the VPS had 4.4 GB of 7.9 GB memory free, 56 GB disk free, 15 containers running, port 8974 unused, and the image pulls successfully.

If yes: two commands to deploy (`scp mcp/docker-compose.yml` and `docker compose up -d` on the VPS) plus one Nginx Proxy Manager host pointing a hostname at it.

If no: retire `mcp/`, `publish-mcp.yml` and the `gate_mcp_corpus_current` preflight gate together in one commit, recorded as DECISIONS.md D-028, rather than keep maintaining a published image with no purpose.

Recommendation: no strong recommendation either way, this is genuinely Phil's call on risk tolerance for the shared VPS; either answer is fine, the current limbo (built, gated, unused, undecided) is the only bad state.

issues.title: Decide: close two public ports on the VPS, Umami and Listmonk (OWNER-ACTIONS.md item 8, never tracked as an issue)
issues.body:
Umami (port 32769) and Listmonk (port 8081) are both reachable directly from the open internet on the VPS, confirmed live 2026-09-17: both answer HTTP 200 from outside, `docker ps` shows them published on `0.0.0.0`, and the host runs no firewall at all (`ufw status` inactive). Analytics and mailing infrastructure should not be publicly addressable. Low likelihood, real consequence.

This used to be unfixable without breaking the site: `site/nginx/default.conf` reached both services through the host's own public address. That dependency is gone: the site's upstreams now point at the Docker bridge (`172.17.0.1`) instead, proved end to end on production (build `8f2400c02ff063f2`, `stats/script.js` serving correctly, `/subscribe` answering 200, a labelled probe event landing in the analytics database). Closing the ports can no longer affect this site.

What Phil needs to do, on the VPS, in each of the two compose files (shared Hostinger-managed stacks used by other sites too, which is why this was not done unattended):

```
ssh root@187.77.25.50
sed -i 's/"32769:3000"/"172.17.0.1:32769:3000"/' /docker/umami-analytics-vi0p/docker-compose.yml
sed -i 's/"8081:9000"/"172.17.0.1:8081:9000"/'   /docker/listmonk-fhzc/docker-compose.yml
cd /docker/umami-analytics-vi0p && docker compose up -d
cd /docker/listmonk-fhzc     && docker compose up -d
```

Check the quoting in each file before running the sed (the port may be written unquoted), then confirm `curl -m 5 http://187.77.25.50:32769/` fails from outside and 6s-success.com still records a visit.

Recommendation: do it. The precondition that used to block this is resolved and verified.

issues.body:
## What I found

This PM check-in (2026-10-09, :10 slot) found zero Claude-authored commits in this repository since `c2565f114` at **2026-10-04 11:19:40Z**. Checked directly, not assumed: `git log --since="2026-10-04T11:21:00Z"` returns 36 commits, every single one authored by `github-actions` (the hourly check-in and social-draft-rotation bots, which run without an agent). No PM check-in, no operator cycle, nothing, for just under 5 days.

Checked `list_triggers` for the three scheduled Routines that drive this repository's autonomous work:

- **6S Success agile PM (:40)**: `last_run.status: FAILED`, `failure_reason: USAGE_LIMIT_REACHED`, fired `2026-10-09T02:40:34Z`.
- **6S Success hourly operator (:43)**: `last_run.status: FAILED`, `failure_reason: USAGE_LIMIT_REACHED`, fired `2026-10-09T02:44:02Z`.
- **6S Success agile PM (:10)**: this session, ran fine.

So the immediate symptom (both other Routines failing on usage limit) is confirmed right now, and the 5-day commit gap says this is not a one-off: whatever caused these two runs to fail has very likely been failing most runs since 2026-10-04 11:20Z, with nothing surfacing it until this cycle happened to check `list_triggers` and the commit history together.

## Why this is worth your attention

Nothing in the product broke: `preflight.py` shows 0 FAIL through every gate it can reach in this sandbox, and the 8 open GitHub issues are unchanged (all `decision`/`blocked-on-art`, already waiting on you). The actual cost is five days where the business had zero autonomous attention: no measurement, no backlog work, no verification, nothing but a bot bumping a check-in log and rotating social drafts, which made the repository look alive in `CHECKIN-LOG.md` while nothing was actually happening.

I cannot see or change your Claude Code usage/plan limits from here; that is the one lever that would fix this, and it is yours to pull.

## Recommendation

Check your Claude Code usage limit / plan status. If this is a recurring resource ceiling (three Routines firing every 30/30/60 minutes is a lot of concurrent usage), consider whether all three need to run that often, or whether the plan needs headroom. Either way, worth building a cheap check (the next operator or PM cycle already has `list_triggers` access) that notices a Routine's `last_run.status == FAILED` and actually surfaces it, rather than relying on a human or a later cycle noticing the commit-author gap by chance, the way this cycle did.

issues.title: Decide: the deck gallery and the deck download are two different card designs
issues.body:
## What I found

`deck.html` and `deck-gallery.html` each do two things: they show the card
gallery, and they link the free print-and-play PDF. Those two are built from
completely different sources and the cards do not look alike.

Verified on the same card, EE-002 "Rainstorm":

- **The gallery** (`site/assets/cards/entryway/`, built by
  `ops/split_deck_cards.py` from your scanned sheets) shows a photographic card:
  a family coming in from rain, five numbered callouts across the picture (Boot
  Tray, Umbrella Station, Waterproof Entry Mat, Wet Coat Zone, Dry Walking
  Path), an Objective block and an Event Effect block.
- **The PDF** (`site/downloads/6S-Entryway-Deck-PrintAndPlay.pdf`, built from
  `ops/build_card_template.py` output) shows a minimal card: red header, title,
  a placeholder glyph where the photograph goes, and one paragraph of In Play
  text.

I identified the PDF card by pixel-matching all 178 embedded images against the
rendered PNG, distance 0.02 out of 255, so this is the same card and not two
cards that happen to share a code.

So a visitor browses one product and downloads another.

## What is and is not already known

The counts on the page are honest. `deck.html` says "89 cards, 72 of them drawn
so far", and the gallery does show 72 after `CANON_EXCLUDE` hides 16 with
retired "Set in Order" text (#29). None of that is in question.

What nothing states is that the two designs differ at all. Separately, 12 of the
89 cards in the PDF have no artwork, which is the subject of the note now in
OWNER-ACTIONS.md and of the `deck-art` warning in preflight.

## Why this is your call and not mine

It is a decision about what the product IS, not a defect with one correct fix.

**Option A: the new template is the product.** Wire
`build_card_template.py`'s output into the gallery so the browsing experience
matches the download. Honest immediately, and it un-hides the 16 cards #29 hides
because the new template sets text as real type rather than baking it into
pixels, so "Set in Order" stops being a pixel problem. Cost: the gallery becomes
visibly plainer, and 12 cards would show a placeholder in public until the art
is regenerated.

**Option B: the scanned sheets are the product.** Rebuild the print-and-play PDF
from the gallery images so the download matches what is shown. Keeps the richer
look. Cost: the text defects stay baked in pixels and cannot be fixed by
generators, and the deck stays at 72 cards.

**Option C: neither yet.** Say on the page that the gallery shows the
illustrated edition and the free download is the typeset one. Cheapest, honest,
and it stops the mismatch being a surprise. It does not remove the mismatch.

## Recommendation

**C now, A after the art is regenerated.** C takes an hour and removes the
surprise. A is the right end state, because the template pipeline is the one
that can be corrected by changing code rather than by redrawing, but running it
today would publish 12 blank cards on the page that is meant to sell the deck.
Enabling image generation (`OWNER-ACTIONS.md`, section 1b, 13.53 dollars) is
what turns A from a downgrade into an upgrade.

I have not changed either surface. Nothing here is broken for a customer today;
it is a mismatch between what is shown and what is delivered, and which way to
resolve it is a product decision.

issues.title: Live deck gallery: 14 cards still say "Set in Order", one is the wrong card entirely
issues.body:
## What I found

Opened 25 of the 88 live cards at `site/assets/cards/entryway/` directly (not the corpus, not a commit message) after noticing EP-005's withholding note also mentioned it "still says Set in Order." That turned out not to be a one-card problem.

**15 cards burn "Set in Order" into the 6S Lesson panel**, the name this repository retired for the second S (D-014, and CLAUDE.md's own "Straighten, never Set in Order"): EM-004, EM-009, EP-001, EP-002, EP-003, EP-006, EP-007, EP-008, EP-010, EP-011, EP-012, ET-009, ET-010, ET-011, ET-012. Every one opened and read directly, not inferred from a count.

**One more, EP-004, is a different and worse defect.** Its file is named `EP-004-Entryway-Backpack-Explosion-front-md.jpg` and its index entry says "Backpack Explosion", but the pixels show a second, uncredited render of the Wet Shoes scene: same rainy doorway, same family, same "6S LESSON: Shine means..." text as the real EP-003. A visitor who opens the Backpack Explosion card sees a duplicate Wet Shoes card instead. No Backpack Explosion art exists anywhere in the live gallery. That makes 16 defective codes in total.

**Two of the fifteen "Set in Order" cards, EP-006 and EP-010, are not in the corpus at all.** This is the same numbering-drift issue #2.7's own backlog note already flags between the corpus (`build/entryway-cardtext.json`) and the live gallery's `index.json`. The corpus's 2026-08-30 fix (commit `4d9401a`, sixteen `six_s_lesson` lines corrected) only reached 13 of these 15 codes for that reason, and never reaches this pipeline anyway (see below).

## Why the corpus fix didn't already cover this

Same root cause as issue #1. `ops/build_card_template.py` (the corrected, text-as-real-type pipeline) writes to gitignored `build/card-fronts/`, which the live site never serves. `site/deck-gallery.html` renders from `site/assets/cards/entryway/index.json`, built by `ops/split_deck_cards.py` from a separate set of scanned sheets on Phil's Desktop that the corpus fix never touched. The print-and-play PDF (`site/downloads/6S-Entryway-Deck-PrintAndPlay.pdf`) is unaffected: I checked it directly (rendered pages 1 and 2 to images) and it is built from the newer, corpus-driven pipeline, correctly says "Straighten," and does not carry this defect.

## What I did

Same mitigation as EE-001/EP-005 in `d0d95de`, extended rather than reinvented: `ops/split_deck_cards.py` now has a `CANON_EXCLUDE` set (16 codes) alongside `BRAND_EXCLUDE`, unioned into `WITHHOLD`. All 16 entries and their image files are removed from `site/assets/cards/entryway/index.json` and disk by hand, since the real source sheets are Desktop-only and unreachable from this sandbox. `preflight.py`'s `gate_deck_art_withheld` now checks the union instead of just `BRAND_EXCLUDE`, proved to fail by temporarily reintroducing one of the codes.

This drops the live, shown gallery from 88 to 72 cards, and the Problem card type specifically from 11 shown to 1 (only EP-009, Mud Trail, was clean). `deck.html`'s counts, spine, and one example card image (it was using EP-001) are corrected to match. This is a real, visible shrink to the free evidence deck, not a rounding change, which is why it is filed rather than just fixed quietly.

## What I did not do

Regenerate the art. Same wall as issue #1 and #2: no Desktop access from this sandbox, no image-generation path here.

## Recommendation

Same as issue #1: either wire `build_card_template.py`'s corrected output into the actual live gallery pipeline, or regenerate these 16 sheets through `split_deck_cards.py`'s own source path with corrected text. Worth doing together with issue #1 and the 2.7 backlog note on the corpus/gallery numbering mismatch, since all three are the same underlying gap: two unconnected art pipelines, one of them fixed and unshipped, one of them shipped and not fixed.

issues.title: Decide: 6S Success and Ledgerium share one Stripe legal entity
issues.body:
## What I found

While branding the checkout page I found the 6S Success Stripe account carrying
another company's identity:

- **Business website: `https://ledgerium.ai`**
- **Product description:** Ledgerium AI's, in full, describing a workflow
  documentation platform
- **Industry: Software**, which is why the MCC is 5734, Computer Software Stores
- **Account representative email: `hello@ledgerium.ai`**

Editing them opens a dialog headed **"Shared legal entity: Changes to this legal
entity will update all accounts that use it."**

## Why it is like that, and why that part is fine

The same dialog says *"Because you selected individual as your business type,
your name is also the legal name of your business."*

So both businesses are you, personally, as a sole proprietor. They genuinely
share a legal entity because there is only one. That is not a misconfiguration,
and Stripe explicitly permits it:

> When you have multiple projects or businesses that operate under the same
> legal entity, you can use the same tax ID and business information across
> multiple accounts. Make sure to provide suitable public business information
> to avoid customer confusion.

They are also already **separate accounts**, which is the part that matters
most. This is `acct_1U5rDs6OlZmKL8mF`, and it has its own products, prices,
payment links, balance and payouts.

## On organizations

You suggested organizations, and it is the right instinct but not the fix here.
Stripe Organizations are a reporting and team-management container:

> An organization doesn't conduct its own business through Stripe. It acts as a
> container structure to view and manage the operation of its separate
> businesses.

An organization would give you one dashboard across both brands, consolidated
reports, and one place to manage team access. Genuinely useful once there are
two revenue streams to compare. It would **not** separate the legal entity or
give each brand its own business profile, because that is not what it does.

## The actual problem, which is smaller than it looked

Not the shared entity. Just the **public information on this account**, which
Stripe says must be per account precisely to avoid the confusion above.

Already fixed, and per account:

| Field | Now |
|---|---|
| Public business name | 6S Success |
| Statement descriptor | 6S SUCCESS |
| Support email | support@6s-success.com |
| Support URL | https://6s-success.com/contact |
| Privacy policy, Terms | the real pages on our site |
| Checkout icon and colours | the site's arc gauge and palette |

**Still wrong: the business website field**, which is what appears on receipts
and in a dispute review. I was blocked from editing it: overwriting a
business-identity field on a live payment account is held back by a safety
check, which I am not going to route around.

## What I need from you

1. **Change the business website to `https://6s-success.com`.**
   Settings, Business details, Public details, Edit. It sits directly under the
   support URL I already filled. **Check whether saving warns that it will
   change Ledgerium too.** If it does, stop and tell me, because that is a real
   trade and not mine to make.

2. **Rewrite the product description**, currently Ledgerium's. There is a
   correct one already written in `STRIPE.md` under "The corrected business
   description", which uses Straighten rather than Set in Order and puts Safety
   fourth.

3. **Consider changing the industry** from Software. 5734 is Computer Software
   Stores, which is wrong for books, card decks and home consulting, and MCC
   affects both interchange rates and fraud scoring. It may trigger a review, so
   it is your call rather than a quiet fix.

4. **Optional: create an organization.** Worth doing when both brands are
   earning and you want one view. Not urgent, and it does not solve any of the
   above.

## Also worth knowing

Checkout currently shows **"6S Success will contribute 1% of your purchase to
removing CO2"**. Stripe Climate is on at 1% of revenue. Keep it or turn it off,
but it should be a decision rather than an inheritance from the other account.

issues.title: Decide: chapter 47's 27 plates are monochrome while the rest of the book is colour
issues.body:
## What was found

Chapter 47, The Mudroom, has 27 finished plates on disk. None are wired into
the chapter and none are on the Mudroom room page. That is not an oversight:
a pass on 2026-08-05 stopped deliberately before wiring and left its reasoning
in `CH47_IMAGE_FINALIZATION_NOTES.md` in the Master folder.

I re-measured it independently today and the earlier finding holds.

Mean per pixel colour saturation:

| Batch | Saturation |
|---|---|
| Chapter 47, all 27 plates | 2.2 |
| Chapter 38, already wired | 54.5 |
| Chapter 39, wired today | 56.5 |

Every chapter 47 plate is a black and white pencil illustration. Chapters 31
to 39 are warm colour photography and colour infographics. That is an order of
magnitude apart, not a variation.

The earlier pass also found two canon violations in the plates it opened, the
clearest being that `image09` recommends a lidded basket to hide clutter,
which contradicts the chapter's own frozen argument that a lid hides the drift
instead of fixing it.

## Why this is yours and not mine

Wiring the plates would commit the book to a mixed visual style by default,
which is a whole book decision. Leaving them out keeps one of 20 rooms
unillustrated. Neither is reversible for free.

## Options

1. **Regenerate chapter 47 in the established colour style.** Keeps Part 9
   coherent. Costs one batch of image generation. This is my recommendation.
2. **Restyle the whole book to monochrome line art.** The illustrations are
   genuinely good and one colour printing is materially cheaper, but this
   orphans the nine chapters already wired plus everything in chapters 1 to 30.
3. **Keep a deliberate mixed style.** I advise against it. It reads as a
   production accident rather than a choice.

Whichever way it goes, the canon violations need fixing before those plates
are used.

## Recommendation

Option 1. The colour family is established across nine wired chapters and the
whole site design system, and one batch is the cheapest way to make chapter 47
match rather than making 40 other things match chapter 47.

issues.title: Decide: 6S Success needs its own Listmonk, or the shared one breaks both brands
issues.body:
## Decision

One Listmonk instance now serves two businesses. Decide whether 6S Success gets its own, or whether the shared one is reconfigured.

## What I found

The `6S Success Readers` list exists and works. I subscribed a test address end to end and Listmonk accepted it and sent a confirmation. Then I read that confirmation out of the mailbox, and it would have broken every signup:

**1. The confirmation link is dead.**

```
http://localhost:9000/subscription/optin/eeb9c298-...
```

That is Listmonk's default Root URL, untouched. `localhost` resolves to the *subscriber's own machine*, so the link cannot work for anybody. With double opt-in enabled, **100 percent of signups would be unconfirmable** and the list would fill with pending addresses that can never be mailed.

**2. The sender is the wrong brand.**

```
From: "Compassion Benchmark" <info@compassionbenchmark.com>
```

Somebody who signs up on 6s-success.com receives mail from an unrelated company. That reads as phishing, and it damages both brands.

## Why it is a decision and not a fix

Root URL and the from address are **instance wide in Listmonk, not per list**. So they cannot be set correctly for two brands at once:

- Point Root URL at `6s-success.com` and every Compassion Benchmark confirmation link breaks.
- Leave it as it is and every 6S Success link stays broken.
- Change the from address either way and one of the two brands sends mail as the other.

Compassion Benchmark is a live business, so I am not touching its settings.

## Options

| Option | Cost | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| **A second Listmonk for 6S Success** | One more container, no licence cost | Each brand gets a correct Root URL and sender. Clean, and the pattern already used for the website and the MCP server. |
| Reconfigure the shared one for 6S | Free | Breaks Compassion Benchmark's confirmation links. Not acceptable. |
| Reconfigure for a neutral sender | Free | Both brands send mail as something that is neither. Worse for trust than either alone. |
| Use a hosted provider for 6S only | Free to 1,000 contacts | Reintroduces the vendor decision that Listmonk had already removed. |

## Recommendation

**A second Listmonk instance for 6S Success**, on its own port behind the proxy, with Root URL set to its public HTTPS address and the sender set to `support@6s-success.com`, which is a mailbox we already control and which already sends.

It costs one container on a VPS already running eight projects, keeps Compassion Benchmark untouched, and means neither brand can ever send mail as the other.

## What I did in the meantime

The newsletter form is **not** pointed at Listmonk. The wiring was written and then deliberately reverted, because a form that produces dead confirmation links is worse than the honest handoff that is there now. The code is in git history at the commit that records this and takes minutes to restore once the instance is correct.

Also: `support@6s-success.com` is on the list as an unconfirmed test subscriber. Harmless, and worth removing when convenient.

## Required response

Approve a second Listmonk instance, or name a different option. Once the instance has a correct Root URL and sender, wiring the form and verifying a real double opt-in end to end is one pass.
